_transcription: ENGLISH half only, CBSE Class 10 Science (086), Series QQARR/1, SET-1, the 2022 Term-II paper, 40 marks, 2 hours, cover says 11 printed pages. PAGE MAP, all 16 rendered indices accounted for: idx 0 cover; idx 1 Hindi instructions + Hindi Q1-4; idx 2 English instructions + Section A Q1-4; idx 3 Hindi Q5-7; idx 4 English Q5-7; idx 5 Hindi Q8-11; idx 6 English Section B Q8-11; idx 7 Hindi Q12-14 (start); idx 8 English Q12, Q13, Section C note, Q14 passage + (a), (b); idx 9 Hindi Q14 (c) + Q15 (folio 10); idx 10, 11, 12, 13 BLANK (identical 11,828-byte renders, idx 10 confirmed blank at full size); idx 14 ENGLISH ONLY (folio 11): Q14 (c)(i) OR (c)(ii) and the whole of Q15; idx 15 BLANK (confirmed at full size). So English = idx 2, 4, 6, 8 and 14; the alternation held through idx 9, then four blank pages sit between the Hindi folio 10 and the English folio 11, so the tail of Q14 and all of Q15 live on an English page with no Hindi partner after it. Odd-page tops (idx 1, 3, 5, 7, 9) all open in Hindi; no English overflow onto any of them. Questions run 1-15 unbroken. STRUCTURE read off the printed English instructions on idx 2 and it matches term2_s10 exactly: 15 questions, three sections; A Q1-7 short answer at 2 marks; B Q8-13 short answer at 3 marks; C Q14-15 case-based at 4 marks; instruction (vi) says internal choices are provided in some questions, with no count. 14 + 18 + 8 = 40. Section C's own note says each case has three sub-questions (a), (b), (c), with (a) and (b) compulsory and an internal choice in part (c). INTERNAL CHOICE roster built by walking the marking scheme (ms p02-p08, every page footed X_51_086_31/1/1, so the scheme is this set's own and not merged): a bare OR after Q5, Q6, Q7, Q9, Q12, Q14 (c) and Q15 (c), and nowhere else; each confirmed against a printed OR on the paper. 7 alternatives, 26 rows (15 primaries + 7 alternatives + 4 extra case-study sub-parts). Case-study part marks as printed: Q14 (a) 1/2+1/2, (b) 1, (c)(i) 1+1, (c)(ii) 1+1; Q15 (a) 1, (b) 1, (c)(i) 2, (c)(ii) 2; each sums to 4. No MCQs, so no key; no void or award-regardless note anywhere in the scheme. No decimal numbers are printed on the paper. PERIODIC CLASSIFICATION: Q2 and Q8 are filed on 'Periodic Classification of Elements [Outdated]' / 'The Modern Periodic Table'; the chapter is declared but not yet live and the axis prints no subtopics for it, so the subtopic name was chosen here (see the rows' _flag). One figure on the paper: the Q11 (b) resistor network (idx 6).

questions._flag: PERIODIC CLASSIFICATION: group numbers in the Modern Periodic Table belong to the old NCERT Class 10 chapter dropped at rationalisation, so this is filed on 'Periodic Classification of Elements [Outdated]'. That chapter is declared in config.ts but not yet live, and axis.ts prints no subtopics for it, so the subtopic 'The Modern Periodic Table' was chosen here from the old chapter's own top-level section heading (Making Order Out of Chaos: The Modern Periodic Table). It is the first 2022 Science paper to need it; sibling sets should reuse this exact name. Parts (b) and (c) also touch ionic bonding (Metals and Non-metals), but the question is framed on the periodic table.
questions.stem:
The electrons in the atoms of two elements X and Y are distributed in three shells having 1 and 7 electrons respectively in their outermost shells.

(a) Write the group numbers of these elements in the Modern Periodic Table.

(b) Write the molecular formula of the compound formed when X and Y combine with each other.

(c) Which of the two is electropositive ?

(a) Which of the following flowers will have higher possibility of self-pollination ?

Mustard, Papaya, Watermelon, Hibiscus

(b) List the two reproductive parts of a bisexual flower.
Which one of the two multicellular organisms — Spirogyra and Planaria reproduces by regeneration and why ? Give an example of any other organism which can also reproduce by the same process.
What is variation ? List two main reasons that may lead to variation in a population.

(i) In a cross between violet flowered plants and white flowered plants, state the characteristics of the plants obtained in the \(\mathrm{F_1}\) progeny.

(ii) If the plants of \(\mathrm{F_1}\) progeny are self-pollinated, then what would be observed in the plants of \(\mathrm{F_2}\) progeny ?

(iii) If 100 plants are produced in \(\mathrm{F_2}\) progeny, then how many plants will show the recessive trait ?

(i) Name and state the rule to determine the direction of force experienced by a current carrying straight conductor placed in a uniform magnetic field which is perpendicular to it.

(ii) An alpha particle while passing through a magnetic field gets projected towards north. In which direction will an electron project when it passes through the same magnetic field ?

What is ozone ? How is it formed in the upper layers of the Earth’s atmosphere ? How does ozone affect our ecosystem ?

(i) List two human-made ecosystems.

(ii) “We do not clean a pond in the same manner as we do in an aquarium.” Give reason to justify this statement.

questions.stem:
(a) List two advantages of adopting the atomic number of an element as the basis of classification of elements in the Modern Periodic Table.

(b) Write the electronic configurations of the elements X (atomic number 13) and Y (atomic number 20).

Draw two different possible structures of a saturated hydrocarbon having four carbon atoms in its molecule. What are these two structures of the hydrocarbon having same molecular formula called ? Write the molecular formula and the common name of this compound. Also write the molecular formula of its alkyne.

(i) Write the molecular formula of benzene and draw its structure.

(ii) Write the number of single and double covalent bonds present in a molecule of benzene.

(iii) Which compounds are called alkynes ?

(a) Mention one function each of the following organs in human male reproductive system :

(i) Testis

(ii) Scrotum

(iii) Vas deferens

(iv) Prostate gland

(b) Name the type of germ cell which (i) is motile, and (ii) stores food.

(a) Three resistors \(\mathrm{R_1}\), \(\mathrm{R_2}\) and \(\mathrm{R_3}\) are connected in parallel and the combination is connected to a battery, an ammeter, a voltmeter and a key. Draw suitable circuit diagram to show the arrangement of these circuit components along with the direction of current flowing.

(b) Calculate the equivalent resistance of the following network :

(i) Define Electric Power and write its SI unit.

(ii) Two bulbs rated 100 W; 220 V and 60 W; 220 V are connected in parallel to an electric mains of 220 V. Find the current drawn by the bulbs from the mains.

(i) State Joule’s law of heating. Express it mathematically when an appliance of resistance R is connected to a source of voltage V and the current I flows through the appliance for a time t.

(ii) A \(5\,\Omega\) resistor is connected across a battery of 6 volts. Calculate the energy that dissipates as heat in 10 s.

(a) Name the group of organisms which form in the first trophic level of all food chains. Why are they called so ?

(b) Why are the human beings most adversely affected by bio-magnification ?

(c) State one ill-effect of the absence of decomposers from a natural ecosystem.

questions.context: The mechanism by which the sex of an individual is determined is called sex-determination. In human beings, sex of a newborn is genetically determined, whereas in some others it is not. There are 46 (23 pairs) chromosomes in human beings. Out of these, 44 (22 pairs) control the body characters and 2 (one pair) are known as sex chromosomes. The sex chromosomes are of two types — X chromosome and Y chromosome. At the time of fertilisation, depending upon which type of male gamete fuses with the female gamete, the sex of the newborn child is decided.
questions.stem: Why is a pair of sex chromosomes in human beings called a mismatched pair in terms of type and size ?
